text: What is heart failure?
Your heart is a muscle

that pumps blood to
every part of your body.
Heart failure is a condition
where your heart muscle doesn't pump blood
around the body properly.
It happens when your heart becomes enlarged,
weak, or stiff.
Heart attack and high blood pressure
are common causes of heart failure.
But there are many others.
Ask your health care team
about the cause of yours.
When your heart is not pumping properly,
less blood is going to your body's important organs.
This can make you feel tired and dizzy.
People with heart failure
may experience shortness of breath,
or feeling puffed after a small amount of effort.
Fluid buildup around the body also happens often.
When the heart pumping function is abnormal,
the body tries to cope
by increasing the amount of fluid in the blood stream.
This fluid can then leak from the blood stream
into the lungs, ankles, legs, or stomach,
where you may notice swelling.
Heart failure is a serious problem.
But with support from family, loved ones,
and your health care team,
you can manage you condition, improve your health,
and make it easier to do the things
that are important to you.
Talk to your doctor
about what has led to your heart failure.
And to learn more about managing heart failure,
watch the other videos in this series.
